Light and sound: G1 to G10

2026-10-22 · What changed is circled in red. Taken from the running app, on stand-ins so nothing was paid for; the "before" shots were taken first, on episode #1. Everything here is drawn or worked out on this computer, and left out when Windows is set to show no animation.

The deck: frosted glass over moving light (G1)

The cloud of light from the lesson page now moves behind the deck too, and every card is a pane of frosted glass over it. Under the pointer a card leans towards it in three dimensions, and its picture is seen through a lens that follows the pointer: the picture swells, its colours part a little at the rim, and a highlight sits above.

A clip done: sparks and a rising note (G3)

Each clip of a batch (voices, pictures, Make it all) throws sparks off its card with a flare, and its tick is a step higher up a five-note scale, travelling left to right. One that does not come out puffs grey smoke with a sour note. While a script is written, motes drift over the placeholders and gather into each as its title arrives (G2); that one only shows with the real script writer, which sends titles as it goes.

The budget as liquid in a glass (G4)

Settings shows the month's spending as liquid filled to how much of the budget is gone. Every confirmation that costs money shows the same glass, with a dashed line where the job would fill it; agreeing pours it in with a pouring sound before the dialog closes. Near the budget it turns amber, over it red, and it boils.

A voice made visible (G5)

Auditioning a clip shows its voice as ribbons of light, low notes on the left and high on the right, read band by band from the recording so they keep exact time; along the bottom each word lights up with a glow as it is spoken.

Rendering: the darkroom, then confetti (G6, G7)

While clips are drawn, a strip of film in the progress panel develops each one like a print under the red safelight, its shadows first, through the grain, and flashes as it is fixed. When the master video is finished, confetti falls in the series colour, near pieces sharp and far ones out of focus, and a fanfare follows the chime.

In the video: the intro's swarm and a made-up sting (G8, G10)

The intro now opens on thousands of points of light spiralling in over the dark, pulled harder to their places in the finished card until they land together at 2.2 s, when the background has risen, then thrown out by the blow, springing back and fading into the real card. With no sting in the kit, one is made to land on the same moment. A whoosh carries the viewer into each new beat, and teaser hook lines drop in and bounce. Frames at 0.3, 1.3, 2.1, 2.2, 2.4 and 3.7 s of the real series intro (its logo and mascot are test pictures in the kit).

In the video: the robot's eyes (G9)

A footage clip's new Look switch shows the film as the R1's camera might see it: brightness as depth in false colour, traced edges, scan lines, corner brackets and a readout with the beat, the clip, a clock and a blinking dot. A film in the Fail beat also glitches and says FAULT. Shown here on a test pattern.
